Description:
Problem:
The repo get and repo delete commands could not accept the native repository path format (/et/<project>/<repo>) that the Entire API returns and that repo clone already accepts. Commands only recognized bare repo names (requiring --project flag) and ULIDs. This created inconsistency: the same path the API gives you back cannot be used directly in other repo commands.
Solution:
Extended resolveRepoRef() to handle slash-bearing native paths by adding a new resolveRepoPathRef() function that parses the /et/<project>/<repo> format. The path parser extracts both the project and repo name from the path itself, so no --project flag is needed. If --project is supplied alongside a path, it is validated for agreement rather than ignored, catching user mistakes. Help text for both commands and the --project flag was updated to document the new path format. Comprehensive tests confirm paths are parsed correctly, optional --project flags are validated, GitHub mirror paths are refused, and the #2252 rule (requiring explicit forge tokens) is enforced at the resolver level.

# Review — trail #1313 / PR #2387 (merged)

**Verdict: correct, and the invariant it claims to preserve actually holds.** I verified it rather than reading it. Findings are all documentation/messaging, no behaviour bugs.

## What I verified (not just read)

Checked out `174dca012` in a scratch worktree and ran probes against the real resolver:

- **#2252 holds at the new resolver.** I fed `TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix`'s own `bare` table into `resolveRepoRef`, plus `github.com/acme/tool`, `https://…`, `git/acme/tool`, `ET/widgets/web`, `//et/widgets/web`. Every one refused locally, **0 HTTP calls**. Nothing is read as a forge it didn't name.
- **The `d8840a8da` follow-up closed the hole properly.** `/web`, `web/`, `paul/dogbark/`, `//et/…` — none reach the by-name lookup with a slash in it.
- **It works end-to-end through cobra, not just at the resolver.** `repo get /et/widgets/web` → `projects?name=widgets` → `projects/<id>/repos?name=web` → `repos/<ulid>`. `repo delete` labels the confirmation `repo /et/widgets/web (01…R5)`. `grant repo list` resolves and reaches `/repos/<ulid>/grants`.
- **No regression is possible.** A slash-bearing ref previously always 404'd server-side (names can't contain `/`), so no working invocation changed meaning.
- Package tests pass at the merge commit. The one failure, `TestRunStatus_CheckpointPushDisabledDestinations`, reproduces on the base `e8780c3ef` — unrelated.

## Findings

**1. The capability landed on 11 call sites; the help text landed on 2.** `resolveRepoRef` is shared by `repo get`, `repo delete`, `repo visibility get/set`, `repo protection list/add/remove`, and `grant repo add/list/remove`. The `--project` string changed for *all* of them to "required when `<repo>` is a **bare** name" — which advertises a non-bare form that seven commands never name. Two are now actively wrong:

- `grant.go:383` — `Long: "…access to a repo (name or ULID)."`
- `grant.go:457` — `Long: "…addressed by name or ULID."`

**2. The `/gh/` refusal message is wrong on at least one of the commands it fires for.** `resolveref.go:238`: *"this command addresses Entire-native repos — manage mirrors with `entire repo mirror`"*. But `repo_protection.go:165` has a purpose-built mirror branch (`repo.Provider == repoProviderGitHub` → `protectionMirrorNote`) — `repo protection list` demonstrably *does* address mirrors, by ULID. What's being refused is the *ref shape*, not the repo. And the pointer is a dead end there and for `repo visibility`: `entire repo mirror` has `get`/`remove`/`collaborators`, no protection or visibility. (Its `get` also takes a bare `owner/repo`, so anyone following the hint has to strip the `/gh/` themselves.)

Edge case in the same check: `declaresForge` is a first-segment prefix test with no shape validation, so `gh/web` — two segments, plausibly a native project named `gh` — is reported as "a GitHub mirror ref" rather than pointed at `/et/gh/web`.

**3. CLAUDE.md still frames the `/et/` grammar as clone-only** (line 101: "`clone` accepts a native `/et/<project>/<repo>` ref, a mirror `/gh/<owner>/<repo>` ref, or a full `entire://` URL"). Nine commands now take the native form — and the *asymmetry* is the part worth recording: the other two shapes are **not** accepted (`/gh/` is refused, `entire://` isn't parsed at all).

**4. The bare-pair suggestion ignores a `--project` the user already gave.** `repo get acme/tool --project widgets` → *"did you mean /et/acme/tool?"*. Follow that literally and the next run fails with *"supplied --project "widgets" does not match the project "acme""*. Two-step error dance.

**5. `resolveref.go:236-240` re-implements `bareRefSuggestions`' native branch** (`repo_clone.go:232`). Narrowing to native-only is *right* here — suggesting `/gh/…` would suggest a ref this very resolver refuses — but that reasoning isn't in the comment, so the next reader sees a near-copy and "fixes" it by calling the shared helper.

**6. `TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix` is still clone-only**, while CLAUDE.md describes it as pinning that no forge-less pair resolves "in either parser or **in the command**". There are nine more commands now. The invariant holds today — I measured it — it just isn't pinned. Feeding the existing `bare` slice to `resolveRepoRef` is a few lines.

## Worth crediting

The `--project` agreement check is the right call (validate rather than ignore) and costs no extra round trip in either branch — the name compare is free, and the ULID compare reuses the project lookup the path needs anyway. The test asserting **zero** calls on a name mismatch and no repo lookup on a ULID mismatch pins that properly.

---

Findings 1 and 3 are the ones I'd actually fix; 2 is a message that will mislead someone. Want me to open a follow-up PR, or post these on the trail?
why does `repo get` even has a project flag?
Good question — let me check whether it's actually load-bearing or just historical.

Because a bare repo name isn't an address, and the control plane has no endpoint that pretends otherwise.

**The mechanism.** The only by-name repo lookup is `GET /projects/{projectId}/repos?name=` (`coreapi.ListProjectRepos`). The project is a *path segment* — you cannot ask "which repo is called `web`" without first naming a project. The other route, `ListRepos(Filter:)`, is keyed on `full_name` (`owner/repo`), so it needs the owning namespace too. Repo names are unique only within a project, so `--project` isn't an option or a filter; it's the missing half of the address.

**The history.** Before `ece9fb3dc` (Paul, 2026-06-23, *"resolve repos by name with --project scope"*), `repo get` took a ULID and nothing else. The flag arrived as the enabling half of by-name addressing across `repo get/delete` and `grant repo add/list/remove` — and it's not specific to `get`: eleven commands share it via `bindRepoProjectFlag` (`repo.go:455`).

**And yes — the trail you just asked me to review makes it redundant.** `/et/widgets/web` carries both facts in one token, and it's the spelling the API hands back. The PR pays for the overlap directly: `projectMismatchErr` plus two comparison branches and two tests (`resolveref.go:250-258`) exist *only* to reconcile two ways of saying the same thing, and the flag's help string had to be reworded on all eleven commands to "required when `<repo>` is a **bare** name" — the flag now describes a fallback.

Worth knowing: the two-call route (`project by name → repo by name in project`) isn't waste. It's the forge-safe lookup. `resolveRepoCellPlacement` (`cell_target.go:372`) builds a bare `owner/repo` filter against the repos index, and `resolveNativeRepoCellPlacement` says outright it "deliberately never consults the forge-blind repos index: that index can select a same-named `/gh/` mirror instead." So the extra round trip buys namespace safety.

**My read on what to do:** don't remove it — `repo get web --project widgets` shipped in June and is presumably scripted somewhere. But it's now the legacy spelling and should stop being advertised as the primary route: document `/et/<project>/<repo>` as the form (it's what the API returns and what `repo clone` already takes), leave the flag working, demote it in help.

If it stays, one inconsistency should go with it: with a **ULID** ref a disagreeing `--project` is silently ignored (`repo.go:451-453`), with a **path** ref it's a hard error. Same flag, same command, two policies — the path behaviour is the right one.

Right — with a ULID it makes *no* sense, and that's the weaker of the two cases, not the stronger one.

**What actually happens.** `resolveRepoRef` short-circuits on the first three lines:

```go
if looksLikeULID(ref) {
    return ref, nil
}
```

`projectRef` is never read. So `entire repo get 01ABC… --project a-project-this-repo-is-not-in` succeeds silently and prints the repo. The flag isn't validated, isn't warned about, isn't consulted — it's discarded.

**And the PR just wrote down the principle that contradicts it.** From its own description: *"If `--project` is supplied alongside a path, it is validated for agreement rather than ignored, catching user mistakes."* A ULID names its owning project *more* definitively than a path does — `coreapi.Repo.OwningProjectId` is a required field, not an optional one. So the same user mistake, expressed against a stronger identifier, is the one that goes uncaught.

**Why it probably ended up that way.** Cost asymmetry. Validating the path form is free — the resolver has to look the project up anyway, so the comparison rides along. Validating a ULID needs `GetRepo` to read `OwningProjectId`, which is an extra round trip for `repo delete`, `grant repo *`, `repo visibility *` and `repo protection *` — they go straight to the operation with the ULID and never fetch the repo. (Not for `repo get`, though: it calls `GetRepo` regardless and already *prints* the owning project as a column. There, the answer is sitting in the response it's about to render.)

But that's an argument against *validating*, not an argument for *silently accepting*.

**The free fix is simpler than either.** `--project` is only ever meaningful for one of the three addressing forms:

| form | self-scoping? | `--project` |
|---|---|---|
| ULID | yes, globally | meaningless |
| `/et/<project>/<repo>` | yes | redundant |
| bare name | no | **required** |

So the coherent rule is: *if the ref names its own project, `--project` adds nothing — say so.* One `if`, no network call, uniform across all eleven commands. That's arguably better than the agreement check the PR added, which spends ~10 lines and two tests reconciling two spellings of a fact rather than telling the user they said it twice.

**The one real cost**, and probably why "ignore" won in June: a script doing `entire repo get "$REPO" --project "$PROJ"` where `$REPO` is sometimes a ULID breaks the day you start rejecting. That's a genuine consideration — it argues for a warning rather than an error on the ULID case, or for a deprecation window.

Either way, the current state is the indefensible middle: the flag is validated where it's redundant and ignored where it's meaningless.

Five things, in the order I'd do them. Total is small — roughly 40 lines plus tests.

## 1. Stop silently ignoring `--project` on a ULID

The indefensible middle. `resolveRepoRef`'s first three lines return before `projectRef` is read, so a flatly wrong project is accepted without a word. Warn on stderr rather than error — the ULID form shipped in June and a script passing the flag unconditionally is plausible; the path form shipped yesterday, so its agreement check has no compat debt and can stay as-is.

~10 lines in `resolveRepoRef`, one test. If you'd rather make it an error, say so — I'd want a release of warning first.

## 2. Fix the two `--help` strings that are now wrong

- `grant.go:384` — `"…access to a repo (name or ULID)."`
- `grant.go:457` — `"…access to a repo (addressed by name or ULID)."`

And name the form once in the shared flag (`repo.go:455`), which all eleven commands render, so the other seven stop advertising a "bare name" fallback without ever saying what the non-bare form is. Doc-only.

## 3. Rewrite the `/gh/` refusal message

Current text: *"this command addresses Entire-native repos — manage mirrors with `entire repo mirror`"*. It's wrong on `repo protection list`, which has a purpose-built mirror branch (`repo_protection.go:165`) and answers with something genuinely useful:

> GitHub mirror: branch protection is governed by the upstream repository. Its default branch is always protected on Entire; no rules can be added here.

So the same repo, addressed by ULID, gets a real answer; addressed by `/gh/` path, gets sent to a subtree that has no protection or visibility commands at all. Make the message about the **ref shape**, not the command, and offer the ULID as the way through — no per-command plumbing needed.

While you're in there: two one-liners. The `#2252` suggestion drops a `--project` the user already supplied (follow it literally and you hit "does not match" next), and the near-copy of `bareRefSuggestions`' native branch needs a comment saying why it isn't the shared helper — narrowing to native is *correct* here, since suggesting `/gh/…` would suggest a ref this resolver refuses, but nothing on the page says so and the next reader will "fix" it.

## 4. One sentence in CLAUDE.md

Line 101 still frames `/et/<project>/<repo>` as clone-only. Nine commands take it now — and the asymmetry is the part worth recording: the *other* two clone shapes are not accepted (`/gh/` refused, `entire://` not parsed).

## 5. Extend the forge-prefix guard past `repo clone`

CLAUDE.md describes `TestCloneRefAlwaysRequiresItsForgePrefix` as pinning that no forge-less pair resolves "in either parser or in the command" — there are nine more commands now.
